fields.title: What is cache and where it lives
fields.keyTakeaway: Cache trades freshness for speed, TTL is the numerical expression of allowable staleness, and the cache key must include the user wherever data is personal.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The exact same data takes 5 milliseconds to arrive one time, and 200 milliseconds the next. What does this depend on?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: [[cache|Cache]] is the cheapest way to speed up a product and the cheapest way to start showing untruths. A PM who does not take part in caching decisions discovers that the price on screen differs from the price at checkout, and does not understand why.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Cache is a fast copy of data so you do not have to go to the source. A [[cache-hit|hit]] means data was found, a [[cache-miss|miss]] means going to the source. The [[hit-rate|hit rate]] determines the value.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: There are several tiers, and they add up:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: The first three matter for products because their behavior is visible to the user.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: The key parameter is **[[ttl|time to live]]**: how long a record is considered fresh. It is also a direct measure of how much outdated data is acceptable. Setting a TTL is a product decision expressed as a number.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *How often does the data change?* If it changes more often than it is read, cache is useless. *What happens if we show stale data?* The same question as for denormalization in `DS2-N1-L2`. A stale product description is fine. A stale price is deception. *Who owns the data?* Personal data in a shared cache risks showing someone else's data. The cache key must include the user ID, and an error here causes a leak.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/rows/0/3: Do not change, version in file name
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/rows/2/3: Changes twice a day, but an error is noticeable
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/rows/3/3: Changes constantly, error is visible to the user
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Cache key incident: the feed was cached without a user ID for forty minutes after release. Some people saw someone else's feed with their recent orders. The leak was small in volume and very bad in essence.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Cache does not fix a slow source, it hides it. On a miss, all the slowness returns — and it usually returns at the worst possible moment, right when the cache has just been cleared.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Cache trades freshness for speed, TTL is the numerical expression of allowable staleness, and the cache key must include the user wherever data is personal.
